RagShortTexts: The Akritai borderers held tax-free military lands, fighting Seljuk nomads across Anatolian.

Variants.Content: The Akritai were hereditary border guards who preserved the Byzantine frontier in Anatolia. Under Emperor John III Doukas Vatatzes, their tax-free military smallholdings were revitalized along the mountain passes. Armed with bows, side-swords, and light peltasts, they checked roving Turkmen nomadic raids.
Songs recounting the mythic exploits of Digenes Akritas inspired these border families. So long as the Nicaean crown respected their fiscal immunities, they held the Anatolian ramparts impenetrable.
Akritai mountain rangers blend seamlessly into limestone scrub. Waiting days beside canyon springs in reversible fleece coats, they drop rockslides upon intruding nomad horsemen.
